correctness.rationale: The deleted-edge distance matrix differs from the Hamming matrix at exactly one symmetric pair; the zero-sum Walsh decomposition converts its powered-distance conditional negativity into one positive-rank-one inequality. An integral representation shows the original nonconstant Walsh modes are strictly negative for p in (0,1). The rank-one criterion supplies the exact scalar equation and one-dimensional critical kernel. Negative-type strictness propagation proves uniqueness, isometric face inclusion proves dimension monotonicity, and dominated convergence of the Walsh integral proves the zero limit. Supplementary checker recomputed graph distances, centered spectra and equality modes through dimension seven and roots through eight.

value.rationale: The unmodified Hamming cube has a stable sharp negative-type exponent one. Deleting precisely one edge is a minimal motivated graph perturbation, yet the resulting threshold falls strictly with dimension and tends to zero. The exact all-dimensional spectral criterion, the rank change at the endpoint, and asymptotic collapse make this a structural Hilbert-embedding instability rather than a routine finite tabulation.
